newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends down after volatile session.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends down after volatile session.

text.p: Convulsions in the Australian dollar led to a volatile session for its New Zealand counterpart on Tuesday, the Kiwi ending about 12 basis points lower after an active day's trade.
By 0500 GMT the Kiwi was at NZ$0.6927/34 from 0.6939/46 at the open, the currency having had a good look at resistance around 0.6950.
The Trade-Weighted Index ended at 68.78 from 68.80.

Dealers expect any short term upside to be limited to 0.6950, depending very much on the fortunes of the Australian dollar, which closed locally at US$0.7756/61 from its New Zealand morning level of 0.7772/77.
The Kiwi market had been caught short in the morning but speculation of impending short covering rallies in the Australian dollar helped push it back up.

News that the Australian Industrial Relations Commission had granted lower paid workers a A$10 a week pay rise, against an expected $12 rise, was seen as a sign to sell the Aussie because of its benign ramifications for inflation.
Going into the close the market appeared a little short Kiwi so dealers expected dips to be bought.
The focus was turning to Australia's CPI report on Wednesday, with a low number likely to raise the possibility of another rate cut.
"I think it's going to be largely dictated by the Australian dollar and I think 0.6950 is pretty well resisted," said one other dealer. Expected range overnight: 0.6915-45.
